### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva 6  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.652)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:17993)

**Proposed mechanism:** TRPM4 (HGNC:17993) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of keratinocyte differentiation and proliferation (GO:0045660); Regulation of keratinocyte differentiation and proliferation (GO:0045660) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal keratinization (HP:0000979); Regulation of keratinocyte differentiation and proliferation (GO:0045660) —LEADS_TO→ Erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva (HP:0031133). Loss-of-function mutations in TRPM4 disrupt the regulation of keratinocyte differentiation and proliferation, leading to the shared phenotypes of abnormal keratinization and erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in TRPM4 with frequencies greater than 1% in gnomAD would refute the hypothesis that TRPM4 loss-of-function causes these diseases. _(variant: HGNC:17993)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TRPM4 in these skin disorders could lead to common therapeutic strategies targeting keratinocyte function or ion channel activity.

#### 2. neuronopathy, distal hereditary motor, autosomal dominant 8  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.396)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3295583)

**Proposed mechanism:** TRPM4 (HGNC:12106) —DISRUPTS→ calcium signaling (GO:0005887); TRPV4 (HGNC:12107) —DISRUPTS→ calcium signaling (GO:0005887); calcium signaling (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ neuropathy (HP:0003691); calcium signaling (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ neuronopathy (HP:0003691). Haploinsufficiency of TRPM4 (causing MONDO:0011474) and TRPV4 (causing distal hereditary motor neuronopathy 8) disrupts normal calcium signaling, leading to overlapping neurological phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in TRPM4 and TRPV4 in individuals diagnosed with MONDO:0011474 and distal hereditary motor neuronopathy 8, respectively, or if genetic variants in these genes show no significant association with either disease in large-scale population studies. _(variant: Any common variants (AF > 0.01) in TRPM4 or TRPV4 associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying the shared role of calcium signaling and TRP channels in these distinct neurological disorders could pave the way for developing therapies that target these pathways for broader therapeutic benefit in neurodegenerative conditions.

#### 3. mucolipidosis type IV  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.387)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3295583)

**Proposed mechanism:** MCOLN1 (HGNC:7529) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal protein trafficking and function (GO:0005741); Lysosomal protein trafficking and function (GO:0005741) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal lysosomal morphology (HP:0000767); TRPM4 (HGNC:12150) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal protein trafficking and function (GO:0005741); Lysosomal protein trafficking and function (GO:0005741) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal lysosomal morphology (HP:0000767). Loss-of-function mutations in MCOLN1 disrupt lysosomal protein trafficking and function, leading to abnormal lysosomal morphology in mucolipidosis type IV. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in TRPM4 disrupt lysosomal protein trafficking and function, leading to abnormal lysosomal morphology in MONDO:0011474. The shared convergence node is the disruption of lysosomal protein trafficking and function, resulting in the phenotypically similar outcome of abnormal lysosomal morphology.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in TRPM4 are found to not impact lysosomal protein trafficking and function, or if the resulting phenotype in MONDO:0011474 is demonstrably distinct from abnormal lysosomal morphology. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying the shared disruption of lysosomal protein trafficking and function as a mechanistic link could enable the development of therapeutic strategies that target this common pathway for both diseases, potentially leveraging existing research or drug development efforts for one disease to benefit the other.

#### 4. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2C  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.383)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3295583)

**Proposed mechanism:** TRPV4 (HGNC:12180) —DISRUPTS→ Ion channel activity and regulation of cellular calcium homeostasis (GO:0005249); TRPM4 (HGNC:12179) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of cellular calcium homeostasis (GO:0005249); Ion channel activity and regulation of cellular calcium homeostasis (GO:0005249) —LEADS_TO→ Peripheral neuropathy (HP:0003489); Regulation of cellular calcium homeostasis (GO:0005249) —LEADS_TO→ Axonal neuropathy (HP:0003389). Mutations in TRPV4 (causing MONDO:0011474) and TRPM4 (causing CMT axonal type 2C) disrupt normal ion channel activity, specifically affecting calcium homeostasis. Dysregulation of cellular calcium in neurons leads to peripheral neuropathy and axonal neuropathy, respectively.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in TRPM4 in individuals diagnosed with MONDO:0011474, or identification of pathogenic variants in TRPV4 in individuals diagnosed with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2C, would challenge the proposed distinct gene causality but could support a shared pathway hypothesis if the variant type (e.g., loss-of-function) is consistent. Conversely, finding no functional overlap in cellular assays between TRPV4 and TRPM4 mutations would weaken the hypothesis. _(variant: Common variants (AF > 0.01) in HGNC:12180 (TRPV4) or HGNC:12179 (TRPM4) that are also identified as pathogenic for either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of ion channel dysfunction and calcium dysregulation in these distinct peripheral neuropathies could lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting ion channel function or calcium buffering mechanisms, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.

**Proposed mechanism:** TRPV4 (HGNC:12180) —INCREASES→ Calcium signaling pathway (P00033); TRPM4 (HGNC:12179) —INCREASES→ Calcium signaling pathway (P00033); Calcium signaling pathway (P00033) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0005604); Calcium signaling pathway (P00033) —LEADS_TO→ Dwarfism (HP:0003501). **Proposed mechanism:** TRPM4 (HGNC:12170) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal calcium homeostasis (GO:0005880); TRPM3 (HGNC:12169) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal calcium homeostasis (GO:0005880); Neuronal calcium homeostasis (GO:0005880) —LEADS_TO→ Regulation of ion channel activity (GO:0019704); Regulation of ion channel activity (GO:0019704) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Regulation of ion channel activity (GO:0019704) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); Regulation of ion channel activity (GO:0019704) —LEADS_TO→ Dysmorphic facies (HP:0001999); Regulation of ion channel activity (GO:0019704) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal anomalies (HP:0002670). **How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic, loss-of-function variants in TRPM4 and TRPM3 in individuals with MONDO:0011474 and neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia, dysmorphic facies, and skeletal anomalies, with or without seizures, respectively, would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if these genes are found to be unrelated to the pathogenesis of either disease, or if the disease phenotypes arise from entirely distinct molecular pathways, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in the coding regions of TRPM4 and TRPM3 in healthy populations would challenge their exclusive role as causal genes for these rare disorders.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic link through TRPM4 and TRPM3 could enable the development of targeted therapies for both disorders by focusing on modulating neuronal calcium signaling or ion channel function.
